title: The Floating Mountains From Avatar Are Real — Zhangjiajie, China | China Travel Expert
description:
The floating mountains from Avatar? They're real — thousands of quartz-sandstone pillars rising out of the mist in Hunan.

Zhangjiajie's pillars were carved by water erosion over more than 380 million years. The most famous — once called the Southern Sky Pillar — stands about 1,080 meters tall and was officially renamed "Avatar Hallelujah Mountain" after the film's creative team drew inspiration from these formations. Zhangjiajie was listed as a UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site (Wulingyuan) in 1992 and became a UNESCO Global Geopark in 2004.

🧭 Expert Tip: Go the morning after rain. The mist pooling between the pillars is exactly the look Avatar chased — and it burns off fast, so start early.
